To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Arrhenius plots of succinoxidase activities in plant mitochondrial fractions were not linear and the slopes of Arrhenius plots for succinoxidase activity of plant tissues varied with the source of the plant tissue, the age of the plant tissue and with the temperature of incubation.

the succinoxidase activity of mitochondria from leaves of Cucurbita pepo and C. moschata is activated by low temperature, while the succinate dehydro-genase activity of these organelles is activated by high temperature.

the mitochondrial succinoxidate and succinate dehyd~ogenase activities are controlled by the same temperature-sensitive factor, that this temperature-sensitive factor is the mitochondrial membrane, and that the mitochondrial membrane is a temperature-sensitive factor because of its lipid composition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of temperature upon mitochondrial respiration.
the effects of the temperature and the concentration of the substrate on the succinoxidase activity of the mitochondrial preparations of some plant tissues.
the effect of temperature on the activity of succinoxidase, succinate dehydrogense, and the cytochrome oxidase systems in plant mitochondria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Arrhenius plots for succinate dehydrogenesis and succinoxidase of plant mitochondria are similar in shape to those of mammalian mitochondria, and that the activation energy is higher for succinate de~ydrogenase than for succinoxidase.

the Arrhenius plots for both succinoxidase activity and succinate dehyd~ogenase activity in mitochondria from a number of plant tissues show that there are two temperature regions of enzyme activity, one below and the other above 30°C, with the break occurring at 30°C.
the Arrhenius plots are linear in all cases studied, and that the activation energies for succinate oxidation and dehydrogenation are the same.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

mitochondrial respiration is a highly regulated and coordinated system that responds rapidly to environmental changes, and that this regulation is accomplished by the coordinated action of a number of enzymes, substrates and metabolites.
we have found a number of mitochondrial activities in a wide variety of plant tissues which have a temperature dependence that is similar to that of mitochondrial activities in animal tissues.
the mitochondrial succinate dehydroxgenase is not a good indicator for plant mitochondrial function and that the succinoxidase is a good indicator for mitochondrial function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Arrhenius plot of mitochondrial succinoxidate activity is linear at temperatures below 30°C and the slope of the line is equal to the activation energy for this process.
mitochondrial succin~dehydrogenase and succinoxidase activities of plant tissues are characterized by the presence of two Arrhenius breaks, one at about 20-25°C and another at about 40°C.
we found that the mitochondrial succinoxidation rate is not a limiting factor for the overall rate of respiration in plant mitochondria.
